priority_gaps:
1. Inadequate number of routine outreach sessions, limiting access to immunization services for underserved and hard-to-reach communities.
2. Inadequate community stakeholder engagement, resulting in limited community participation and support for health interventions.
3. Absence of a structured schedule for Health Educators to conduct ACSM activities, leading to inconsistent health education and community sensitization.
4. Inadequate defaulter-tracking mechanisms in some health facilities, resulting in missed opportunities to identify and follow up with children who default from routine immunization.
supervisor_comment: Overall, there are gaps in routine immunization demand generation, community engagement, outreach service delivery, and defaulter tracking mechanisms. These gaps may contribute to low access to immunization services, missed eligible children, and poor follow-up of defaulters. Strengthening outreach planning, engaging community stakeholders, scheduling regular ACSM activities by Health Educators, and establishing functional defaulter-tracking mechanisms at health-facility levels are recommended to improve RI coverage and reduce the number of zero-doseunder-immunized children.
